clue.text: A day one's works are up to scratch

explanation.surface: Someone's output on a single day passes muster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', giving I + S.
explanation.definitionFit: Something up to scratch meets the required standard, so it is adequate or acceptable.

clue.text: Cast including one bishop's brother or sister

parts.note: to sling is to throw or cast

explanation.surface: A theatre cast that includes a cleric's sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests actors but is the verb throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibling is a child of the same parents.

clue.text: Bloomer made by university student in extremity

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is literally a plant that blooms, and this spring bulb flowers.

clue.text: Moves smartly up coast in the spray

parts.note: to nip is to move quickly

explanation.definitionFit: Spindrift is sea spray blown from wave crests.

clue.text: A private secretary has the key in the recess

parts.note: PS stands for private secretary

explanation.surface: An assistant keeps the key to an alcove.

clue.text: One is in order to keep quiet as a rule

definitions.text: One is in order to keep quiet as a rule

parts.words: One is in order to keep quiet as a rule
parts.note: a member of a religious order whose rule demands silence

explanation.surface: Someone stays quiet as a matter of habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' is a monastic order and 'rule' its monastic rule, not orderliness and habit.
explanation.definitionFit: These Cistercian monks are known for their vow of silence.

clue.text: Leader of robbers, superior to a pirate

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: over means above or superior to

clue.text: Plant to wire as it develops

explanation.surface: A method a conjuror relies on.
explanation.definitionFit: The decimal measurement standard of metres and grams.

clue.text: It's loosely citable as an area of low salinity

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quotable fact about a body of water that is not very salty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loosely' rearranges the letters of CITABLE AS.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern European inland sea is famously brackish, its water much less salty than the open ocean.

clue.text: Say nothing when surrounded by depravity

indicators.note: the zero is placed inside the word for depravity, enclosed by it

parts.note: vice is wickedness or depravity

explanation.surface: Advice to keep quiet when among wicked people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is a noun here: having a say means having a voice.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a say in a matter is to have an opinion heard, an expression of view.

clue.text: Hinder exercises in Mideast, perhaps

PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Something obstructs military drills in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: Mideast is read as Mid-E, E being the usual abbreviation for east; 'perhaps' signals the rearrangement and 'in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To hinder is to obstruct or hold back progress.

clue.text: Speculator who does his job through his connections

definitions.meaning: a stock-market dealer who trades speculatively

definitions.text: who does his job through his connections
definitions.meaning: a telephone switchboard worker who puts calls through by making connections

explanation.surface: A financier who succeeds thanks to friends in high places.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests nepotism; the second reading is literal telephone connections.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a shrewd market dealer and a switchboard worker linking callers.

clue.text: Initial move of doctor in carriage

indicators.note: the doctor's letters go inside the word for carriage

parts.note: carriage here means bearing, the way one walks, gait

explanation.surface: A physician makes the first move while riding in a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage' suggests a vehicle but means deportment or gait.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess opening sacrificing material is the classic opening ploy, hence any first manoeuvre.

clue.text: Dandy endlessly consuming round biscuit

explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims MACARONI to MACARON; 'consuming' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a small almond biscuit.

clue.text: Abstruse notes in a Victorian novel

so (soh) and te are notes of the sol-fa scale
so (soh) and te are notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Obscure annotations found in a nineteenth-century book.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric, or Little by Little is an old moralising boarding-school story, well known in its day; 'in' puts the sol-fa notes inside its title.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a select few, hence obscure or difficult.

clue.text: Merchant does business on the island

parts.note: trades means deals or does business
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A trader runs a business on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman is a shopkeeper or dealer.

clue.text: It transmits information freely to most rich men

clue.text: To a former partner, issuing a subpoena is stimulating

clue.text: Domain in France is swallowed up

clue.text: Block request for table-linen

to ask is to request

clue.text: Lively party providing joints at a higher price

prices are up when they rise

clue.text: Ploughman without time for a book

parts.note: a tiller is one who tills the soil
HR is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time

explanation.definitionFit: A suspense novel full of tension is one kind of book.

clue.text: Wooden strip protecting top of counter in bar

clue.text: A member may be involved in this run

clue.text: Unattractive boy, head of school, embracing a maiden
